title: (RHEA-2014:1740) thermostat1 bug fix and enhancement update
portal_summary:
Updated thermostat1 packages that fix several bugs and add various enhancements
are now available as part of Red Hat Software Collections 1.2 for Red Hat
Enterprise Linux.

portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

This update is available via the Red Hat Network. Details on how to
use the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at
https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258
portal_description:
Thermostat is a monitoring and instrumentation tool for the OpenJDK HotSpot Java
Virtual Machine (JVM) with support for monitoring multiple JVM instances.
Thermostat supports monitoring and gathering performance data from JVMs running
on the same machine, a remote machine, or across a network. The tool consists of
two processes: an Agent, which collects data, and a Client, which allows users
to visualize collected data. These components communicate over a MongoDB-based
storage layer. A pluggable agent and GUI framework allow users to collect and
visualize performance data beyond what is included out of the box.

The thermostat1 packages have been upgraded to upstream version 1.0.4, which
provides a number of bug fixes and enhancements over the previous version.
(BZ#1096078)

This update also fixes the following bug:

* Previously, an attempt to rebuild the thermostat1-felix-framework package
failed due to a missing dependency on the thermostat1-felix-osgi-compendium and
thermostat1-felix-osgi-core packages. With this update,
thermostat1-felix-osgi-compendium and thermostat1-felix-osgi-core are provided
by the maven30 Software Collection. As a result, the user is now able to rebuild
thermostat1-felix-framework after installing the thermostat1-scldevel package
with Red Hat Software Collections 1.2 channels enabled. (BZ#1111677)

Users of thermostat1 are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix
these bugs and add these enhancements.
